about.size: Relatively common at 50-75 lb and can exceed 100 lb
about.diet: Almost totally fish: mackerels, butterfishes, scads, jacks, flying fish; a little squid
about.swimming_depth: Mostly in the upper mixed layer. Tagging off Baja California found an average depth of about 18 m, with 99% of daytime above the thermocline.
about.behavior: Solitary or in very small loose groups. More common near banks (lumps), drop-offs or weed lines in blue water, along current edges and temperature breaks. Not warm-blooded.
about.timing_note: Angler lore: patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies. Numbers are judgment calls to be calibrated against trip logs.

reasons.text: Part of this area overlaps Davis Reef Sanctuary Preservation Area, Conch Reef Sanctuary Preservation Area, where recreational fishing is prohibited. Stay outside the marked zone.
The seafloor drops steeply here (116.0 m of depth change per km), one of the sharper ledges in the area.
Water is 23.6 C, inside the 23-28 C range where wahoo are most active.
The Gulf Stream's inshore edge is close (9 km east of it, inside the stream). Wahoo patrol current edges.
It is wahoo season off South Florida (about October to March).
No chlorophyll reading here today (cloud cover or missing scene), so this score leans on temperature and depth.
